title: Scheduler adaptive-damping to prevent burst propagation and kernel-swap thrash
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: After a scheduler heuristic change (shipped 2026-03-05) that increased per-request kernel probing to optimize average latency for small batches, production traffic experienced multi-minute throughput oscillations and elevated p95/p99 tail latency for multi-tenant customers. The observed pattern was repeated kernel-swap churn during bursts which led to frequent KV-cache invalidations, batch eviction, and degraded throughput for downstream routes.

Root cause: The scheduler's new aggressive probe policy recomputed kernel ranking on every request path boundary and allowed immediate handoffs when an alternate kernel showed marginally lower microbenchmarks. Under bursty multi-tenant load this produced many near-simultaneous kernel swaps on shared GPUs. Swapping kernels evicted warm KV cache entries and caused small batches to miss batching windows, amplifying latency. A contributing factor was the attention autotiling heuristic that chooses split strategies per micro-batch; slight differences in autotiling made certain kernel variants incompatible with existing batch aggregation assumptions, increasing eviction frequency.

Impact: Incident window 2026-03-06 02:10Z to 2026-03-06 02:48Z for east-us region; estimated affected qps: ~12% of hosted API; customer-facing errors were limited but latency regressions triggered SRE alerts and several on-call escalations.

Evidence & artifacts:
- Grafana latency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/latency?from=2026-03-06T02:00Z&to=2026-03-06T03:00Z
- Kernel-change timeline correlating swaps: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/kernel-swap-20260306
- Repro benchmark notebook (synthetic multi-tenant bursts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XYZ-repro-notebooks
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6193 (scheduler probe policy), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6221 (autotile tweak)
comments: 2026-03-06 03:10 - Initial incident triage: SRE noted repeating p95 spikes and high kernel-swap rate. Triage owner: Maya. Immediate rollback planned for probe policy toggle.

2026-03-06 03:45 - Emergency mitigation: rolled back the probe policy flag to conservative mode (no per-request re-ranking). Latency improved within 10 minutes but background churn persisted on a subset of pods. On-call: Diego.

2026-03-07 09:00 - Deep-dive meeting: Eng, SRE, and Runtime teams reviewed traces. Consensus: need middle-ground 'damping' layer in scheduler to prevent simultaneous swaps and add hysteresis before committing kernel handoffs.

2026-03-08 11:30 - Experiment 1: implemented token-window-based damping that requires a kernel candidate to show consistent improvement across N=3 sequential batches before swap. Deployed to canary (10% traffic). Observed decreased swaps and stable p95, small increase in avg latency for tiny requests. Postmortem note: tuning N matters per model family.

2026-03-10 15:20 - Design review: Product and PM (Arjun Patel) agreed that minor avg latency regressions are acceptable if tail and throughput stabilize. Added rollback hooks and telemetry gates to the rollout plan.
2026-03-12 17:50 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6302 implementing adaptive damping + metrics export. Requesting review from runtime-platform and perf teams.

2026-03-13 09:05 - Perf team feedback: add explicit KV-cache warming signal and delay swaps if recent warmup activity detected. Also suggested a 'soft-lock' per-GPU for 200ms during bursts to serialize expensive swaps.
2026-03-14 10:00 - Current status: Diego implementing soft-lock and KV-warmup signal; running extended canary with model groups: text-gen-medium and chat-long-context. Next sync scheduled 2026-03-16.
Action owners: Diego (implementation, ENG-349821), Priya Kapoor (perf testing and benchmarks), Arjun Patel (product sign-off), SRE on-call rotation (rollout & monitoring).
